name: LuaGlobals
simple: Lua globals are the built-in functions that come with the Luau language itself, ready to use in any script without `game:GetService`. They include `print` to show messages, `pairs` and `ipairs` for loops, `pcall` to catch errors, `tonumber`/`tostring` to convert values, and `require` to load ModuleScripts.
analogy: Lua globals are like the basic tools that come in every toolbox before you buy anything extra: a hammer (print), a screwdriver (pairs), a measuring tape (type). Every script has them.
whenToUse: Show messages in Output while testing (`print`).
Go through every item in a table (`pairs`, `ipairs`).
Run risky code safely, like data store calls (`pcall`).
Turn text into numbers and back (`tonumber`, `tostring`).
Load shared code from a ModuleScript (`require`).
where: Available everywhere: Scripts, LocalScripts and ModuleScripts. Just type the name, for example `print("hi")`.

terms.global: Something you can use anywhere in any script without getting it first, like `print`.
terms.function: A named set of instructions you can run, like `print("hi")`.
terms.argument: A value you give to a function inside the parentheses. In `print("hi")`, "hi" is the argument.
terms.return: What a function hands back. `tonumber("5")` returns the number 5.
terms.table: Luau's container for many values. A list like `{"a", "b"}` or a dictionary like `{coins = 10}`.
terms.nil: Luau's word for nothing or no value.
terms.error: When something goes wrong and a script stops with a red message in Output.
terms.pcall: Short for 'protected call'. Runs a function and catches errors, so your script keeps going.
terms.iterator / loop: A `for` loop that goes through items one by one. `pairs` and `ipairs` help a loop walk through a table.
terms.metatable: A secret helper table that changes how another table behaves, for example what happens when you add two tables. Advanced.
terms.metamethod: A special function in a metatable, like `__index` or `__tostring`, that Roblox runs in certain situations. Advanced.
terms.ModuleScript: A script that holds shared code. Other scripts load it with `require` and get back what it returns.
terms.Output: The Studio window (View > Output) where `print`, `warn` and errors show up.

examples.title: The everyday globals in one script
examples.code:
local scores = { Ava = 30, Ben = 12 }
local fruits = { "apple", "banana", "cherry" }

-- pairs: every key and value in a dictionary (any order)
for name, score in pairs(scores) do
	print(name, score)
end

-- ipairs: a list in order 1, 2, 3...
for index, fruit in ipairs(fruits) do
	print(index, fruit)
end

-- tonumber / tostring
local typed = "42"
local n = tonumber(typed) -- 42 as a number, or nil if it is not a number
print(n + 1) --> 43
print("Score: " .. tostring(n)) --> Score: 42

-- pcall: catch an error instead of crashing
local ok, message = pcall(function()
	error("Oops!")
end)
print(ok, message) --> false  ...Oops!

-- type: what kind of value is this?
print(type(fruits)) --> table
explain: `pairs` goes through every key/value pair in a table.
`ipairs` goes through a list from 1 upward, in order.
`tonumber` turns text into a number (or nil if it cannot).
`pcall` runs a function safely; if it errors, you get false and the error message instead of a crash.

gotchas: In modern Luau you can loop over a table directly: `for key, value in myTable do`. `pairs`/`ipairs` still work fine.
`tonumber` returns nil for text that is not a number, so check before doing math with it.
`pcall` returns `false` plus the error on failure. Do not ignore the first value.
Use `typeof` (a Roblox global) instead of `type` to tell Roblox types apart, like Vector3 vs Part.

_G.simple: A shared table every script on the same side (all server Scripts, or all of one player's LocalScripts) can read and write. A quick way to share values, but a ModuleScript is usually cleaner.
_G.example:
-- Script A in ServerScriptService
_G.gameMode = "Hard"

-- Script B in ServerScriptService (runs later)
task.wait(1)
print(_G.gameMode) --> Hard
_G.gotcha: Server `_G` and client `_G` are separate. It also depends on which script runs first. Prefer ModuleScripts.

_VERSION.simple: A text value (not a function) that says which language version is running. In Roblox it prints something like `Luau`.

assert.simple: Checks that something is true. If it is false or nil, it stops the script with an error message you choose. Great for catching mistakes early.
assert.example:
-- Any script
local part = workspace:FindFirstChild("Door")
assert(part, "Could not find the Door part!") -- errors if part is nil
print("Found the door")

collectgarbage.simple: Old — it only works with "count" in Roblox; use gcinfo() to see memory use instead.

error.simple: Stops the current code on purpose and shows an error message. Often used with `pcall` to report problems.
error.example:
-- Any script
local function setSpeed(speed)
	if type(speed) ~= "number" then
		error("speed must be a number!")
	end
	print("Speed set to", speed)
end

local ok, err = pcall(setSpeed, "fast")
print(ok, err) --> false  ...speed must be a number!

gcinfo.simple: Tells you how much memory your scripts are using right now, in kilobytes (KB). Useful for spotting leaks while testing.
gcinfo.example:
-- Any script
print("Lua memory used: " .. gcinfo() .. " KB")

getfenv.simple: Old — don't use it; it slows scripts down. Use ModuleScripts and local variables instead.

getmetatable.simple: Gets the metatable (secret helper table) of a table, if it has one. Advanced; used when building your own object types.
getmetatable.example:
-- Any script
local helper = { __index = { greet = function() return "hi" end } }
local obj = setmetatable({}, helper)
print(getmetatable(obj) == helper) --> true

ipairs.simple: Used in a `for` loop to go through a list in order: item 1, item 2, item 3... It stops at the first gap (nil).
ipairs.example:
-- Any script
local players = { "Ava", "Ben", "Cy" }
for index, name in ipairs(players) do
	print(index, name) --> 1 Ava, 2 Ben, 3 Cy
end

loadstring.simple: Turns text containing Luau code into a function you can run. It is turned off by default for safety, and only the server can turn it on.
loadstring.example:
-- Script in ServerScriptService (only if LoadStringEnabled is on)
local fn = loadstring("return 2 + 3")
if fn then
	print(fn()) --> 5
end
loadstring.gotcha: Running code from players is very dangerous. Almost every game should leave this off.

newproxy.simple: Makes a blank special object (userdata). Advanced; sometimes used as a unique marker or with a metatable for custom behavior.
newproxy.example:
-- Any script
local marker = newproxy()
print(type(marker)) --> userdata

next.simple: Gets the next key and value from a table after the one you give it. `pairs` uses it under the hood. A common trick: `next(t) == nil` means the table is empty.
next.example:
-- Any script
local bag = {}
print(next(bag) == nil) --> true, the bag is empty
bag.apple = 1
print(next(bag)) --> apple 1

pairs.simple: Used in a `for` loop to go through every key and value in a table, including dictionaries. The order is not guaranteed.
pairs.example:
-- Any script
local inventory = { Sword = 1, Potion = 3 }
for itemName, count in pairs(inventory) do
	print(itemName, count)
end

pcall.simple: Runs a function in 'safe mode'. If the function errors, your script does not crash; instead `pcall` returns false and the error message. If it works, it returns true plus the function's results. Use it for anything that can fail, like data stores and web requests.
pcall.example:
-- Script in ServerScriptService
local DataStoreService = game:GetService("DataStoreService")
local store = DataStoreService:GetDataStore("PlayerCoins")

local ok, result = pcall(function()
	return store:GetAsync("User_1")
end)
if ok then
	print("Loaded:", result)
else
	warn("Failed:", result) -- result is the error message here
end
pcall.gotcha: Only the code inside the function is protected. Keep the risky call inside it.

print.simple: Shows values in the Output window. The number one tool for checking what your code is doing. You can give it many values separated by commas.
print.example:
-- Any script
local coins = 10
print("Hello!")
print("Coins:", coins) --> Coins: 10

rawequal.simple: Checks if two values are exactly the same thing, ignoring any custom `==` rules from metatables. Advanced.

rawget.simple: Reads a value from a table directly, skipping any metatable tricks like `__index`. Advanced.
rawget.example:
-- Any script
local defaults = { speed = 16 }
local settings = setmetatable({}, { __index = defaults })
print(settings.speed)          --> 16 (borrowed from defaults)
print(rawget(settings, "speed")) --> nil (not really inside settings)

rawlen.simple: Gets the length of a table or string, skipping any custom `__len` rule. Advanced.

rawset.simple: Puts a value into a table directly, skipping any `__newindex` metatable trick. Advanced.
rawset.example:
-- Any script
local t = setmetatable({}, { __newindex = function() print("blocked!") end })
t.a = 1          --> blocked!
rawset(t, "a", 1) -- really stores it
print(t.a)       --> 1

require.simple: Runs a ModuleScript and gives you what it returns (usually a table of functions). Runs the module only the first time; later requires on the same side get the same table.
require.example:
-- ModuleScript named "MathHelpers" in ReplicatedStorage:
-- local MathHelpers = {}
-- function MathHelpers.double(n) return n * 2 end
-- return MathHelpers

-- Script in ServerScriptService
local ReplicatedStorage = game:GetService("ReplicatedStorage")
local MathHelpers = require(ReplicatedStorage:WaitForChild("MathHelpers"))
print(MathHelpers.double(21)) --> 42
require.gotcha: The server and each client get their own separate copy of a module. Changing it on one side does not change the other.

select.simple: Picks values from a list of arguments. `select(2, a, b, c)` gives b and c. `select("#", ...)` counts how many there are.
select.example:
-- Any script
print(select(2, "a", "b", "c"))   --> b c
print(select("#", "a", "b", "c")) --> 3

setfenv.simple: Old — don't use it; it slows scripts down. Use ModuleScripts and local variables instead.

setmetatable.simple: Gives a table a metatable (secret helper table) that changes how it behaves. Used to make your own object types with shared functions. Returns the same table.

tonumber.simple: Turns a value into a number if it can. `tonumber("12")` gives 12. If it cannot, you get nil. You can also give a base, like 16 for hex.
tonumber.example:
-- Any script
print(tonumber("12") + 1) --> 13
print(tonumber("hello")) --> nil
print(tonumber("ff", 16)) --> 255

tostring.simple: Turns any value into text. Useful for joining numbers or nil into a message with `..`.
tostring.example:
-- Any script
local score = 99
print("Score: " .. tostring(score)) --> Score: 99
print(tostring(nil)) --> nil

type.simple: Tells you the basic kind of a value as text: "number", "string", "boolean", "table", "function", "nil", "userdata" and a few more. For Roblox things it just says "userdata", so use `typeof` for those.
type.example:
-- Any script
print(type(5))        --> number
print(type("hi"))     --> string
print(type(workspace)) --> userdata (use typeof to get "Instance")

unpack.simple: Takes the items out of a list and gives them as separate values. `unpack({1, 2, 3})` gives 1, 2, 3. Same as `table.unpack`.
unpack.example:
-- Any script
local colors = { 255, 128, 0 }
local c = Color3.fromRGB(unpack(colors))
print(c)

xpcall.simple: Like `pcall`, but you also give an error handler function that runs when something goes wrong, for example to add extra details to the error.
